Senses.Explanation: Within the Caodong Five Ranks, coming from within the absolute (正中來) names a movement from the upright or correct position; Caoshan describes it as words within no-words, without setting up rank or falling to either side. Caoshan Benji explains the label through coming from the correct position and gives examples of speech within no-speech. Hongzhi Zhengjue's verse pictures a great fish shedding its shell and taking the bird path, while an unnamed monastic later asks Fenyang Shanzhao for the rank and receives the image of lotuses opening on dry ground. Langting Ting pairs the rank with partridge calls and opening flowers. Juelang Daosheng later explains it through a ruler at the highest point, Yongjue Yuanxian gives a midnight plum opening against snow, and Ruibai Mingxue classifies a shout free of names and words as this rank. These changing images and schemata illustrate one named relation rather than establish separate senses.

Senses.Explanation: Within the Caodong Five Ranks, the relative within the absolute (正中偏) names differentiated appearance within the absolute or upright. Records identify it relationally and then test it through verses, images, and contrast with the absolute within the relative (偏中正). Caoshan Benji explains that the upright position is the empty realm and the partial position the realm of forms; he glosses the relative within the absolute (正中偏) as turning from principle toward affairs and elsewhere as the lord looking toward the minister. Hongzhi Zhengjue's Five Ranks verse gives the rank a night image in which a wooden boy strikes the moon's door and wakes a jade woman. The Mirror of Humans and Devas records an unnamed monastic asking Fenyang Shanzhao for this rank and preserves Fenyang's moon-and-cock response. Langting Ting gives it swallows murmuring between roof beams. Juelang Daosheng relates it to an eastern circle and lesser yang, while Ruibai Mingxue identifies his own shout as this rank once he has mounted the seat. Tianran Hanshi transmits an older night-and-moon verse whose historical author is not established in the available six-rung evidence and then offers his own matching verse, showing that no single image exhausts the relation.

Senses.Explanation: The authoritative command is something the records enact, raises, or demands in force, commonly in military and public-command language. The authoritative command currently being carried out or brought fully into effect. The term occurs 1,503 times in 291 allowlisted texts. Chan records place this governmental and military command language on the public teaching seat: a questioner asks what Fenyang Shanzhao will show ‘when the command is carried out’; Longtan Yuan declares that ‘the command has already been carried out’; Rui'an Sengyin associates Yunmen Wenyan's command with blows that distinguish dragons from snakes; and Baichi Yuan describes Baoshou as commanding within the realm and holding authority beyond the gate. Stock forms include ‘the command is put into effect’ ( in ), ‘fully bring forward the command’ (170 in 103), and ‘the command has already been carried out’ (28 in 23). Chengtian Que also criticizes even ‘raising the command's guiding principle’ as making an artificial nest, showing that criticism and exercise can take the same command as their object.

Senses.PreferredTarget: the true eye of the teaching
AlternateTargets: the eye that recognizes the true teaching
Senses.Explanation: The true eye of the teaching, a claimed capacity for recognizing and carrying the lineage's teaching. Bodhidharma tells Huike that it passed from the Buddha through Kasyapa and successive ancestors before reaching him. Later public exchanges refuse to turn that claim into a stable object: Ying'an Tanhua asks for it and Mi'an Xianjie answers with a broken sand basin; Fengxue Yanzhao says to blind it immediately; Guangfa Yuan locates it below the eyebrows, Hanzhushan Shenzhe at the spirit tree before the gate, and Liangshan Yuanguan in Nanhua. Feiyin Tongrong speaks of opening it in the dust of ordinary life. Chan thus treats the eye as both a transmission claim and something that must survive sharply incompatible public answers.
Senses.Note: Frozen-corpus concordance: 2,597 substring hits in 355 files and 349 independent works in the canonical f001 preflight. The longer compound meaning the treasury of this true eye dominates the count; every curated occurrence here was independently filtered to require the standalone headword. Transmission, opening, locating, and blinding are predicates of one claimed eye, not separate things.

Senses.PreferredTarget: the treasury of the true eye of the teaching
AlternateTargets: the treasury of the true teaching eye
SearchAliases: treasury of the true eye of the teaching
Senses.Explanation: The phrase names what lineage narratives claim is possessed, entrusted, preserved, or destroyed in transmission. Shakyamuni Buddha says he possesses it and entrusts it to Mahakasyapa. Wumen Huikai turns that founding claim into a challenge by repeatedly asking how it could be transmitted. Buddhanandi entrusts it to his successor with an injunction not to let it be cut off. At death Linji Yixuan tells the assembly not to destroy his treasury; Sansheng Huiran replies that he would not dare, but after Sansheng's shout Linji says it will perish with this blind donkey. Another lamp passage again quotes Shakyamuni entrusting it to Mahakasyapa. The phrase is therefore an asserted lineage possession whose transmission is both ritually declared and sharply interrogated.
Senses.Note: Exact frozen-corpus count: 1,617 hits in 307 files and 301 works. Seven exact witnesses across four works meet the packet floor and cover founding entrustment, transmission challenge, continuity injunction, deathbed test, reply, reversal, and later restatement.

Senses.Explanation: The true eye is an eye described as correct or authoritative, especially the capacity by which an encounter or saying is distinguished without being fooled. Questions ask for the monastic’s true eye, addresses say it opens or circulates, and the thousand-hand case asks which eye is the true one; these predicates keep eye-imagery and discernment together.

Senses.PreferredTarget: monastic robe, bowl, and personal effects
Senses.Explanation: The material monastic robe, alms bowl, and, by extension, personal effects kept with them. The allowlisted corpus has 513 hits in 115 texts, including records in which the objects are thrown onto a rock, lifted, carried, guarded, inventoried, or burned with a person's other implements. Monastic regulations also name a ‘robe-and-bowl attendant’ (衣鉢侍者, 9 hits in 3 texts), who receives the seal in one installation procedure. In the Caoqi record, this attendant raises the robe associated with the object that could not be lifted at Dayu Ridge. These passages keep the material objects and their custodial office visible even where the same pair also marks succession.
Senses.Note: This first sense covers the material pair and its administrative extension to personal effects and the attendant responsible for them. It is separated from the succession-token sense because regulations can order the objects burned or placed in custody without describing succession.

Senses.PreferredTarget: the robe and bowl as evidence of lineage succession
Senses.Explanation: The same physical robe and bowl treated as passed evidence of lineage succession. The corpus records ‘transmit the robe and bowl’ (傳衣鉢, 31 hits in 26 texts), ‘entrust the robe and bowl’ (付衣鉢, 10 hits in 8 texts), and one exact occurrence of ‘robe and bowl transmitted in succession’ (衣鉢相傳). The Dayu Ridge account explicitly calls the robe ‘a token of trust.’ Yuansou Xingduan says that Huangmei's robe and bowl were entrusted to Lu, while Qining Wenyi asks which robe and bowl Lu actually transmitted. The question is recorded as a question rather than resolved here into an object different from the material robe and bowl.
Senses.Note: Historical succession does not make this sense specific to a named individual. The selected passages show the physical token, later transmission language, and a later challenge about what was transmitted. The seven required definition formulas were searched; no additional lexical self-definition was found.
